name: Octi Zhang

papers.title: A Balanced Data Diet: Addressing the Bottleneck in Mega-Scale RL for Robot Control
papers.abstract: General-purpose robots must perform a wide range of tasks from agile locomotion to dexterous manipulation, but current sim2real RL pipelines depend on per-task structural priors to train such as shaped rewards and demonstrations. Recent work has shown that diverse simulator resets, combined with massively parallel simulation, can replace much of this engineering. Yet, uniformly sampling over this distribution wastes a growing fraction of environments on task configurations the policy has already mastered or cannot yet attempt, so returns flatten when scaling the number of parallel environments. We introduce a simple adaptive sampler, Success Guided Sampling (SGS), that tracks the policy's frontier of capability, concentrating experience on task configurations where success rate sits in a productive band. This results in continued performance gains up to 1M+ parallel environments, 16× beyond prior work, under simple reward structures and no demonstrations. We demonstrate this on two settings where prior approaches required per-task engineering. For agile locomotion, a single policy acquires multiple long-horizon skills that previously demanded per-task priors and separate training runs. For dexterous manipulation, we present the first fully-RL solutions to the nut-and-bolt and rod assembly tasks from the NIST board.

papers.title: ADEPT: Accelerating Dexterity via Pre-Training and Post-Training using Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: We introduce Accelerating DExterity via Pre-Training (ADEPT), a framework for learning high degree-of-freedom (DoF) arm-hand dexterity through large-scale RL. ADEPT pretrains a dexterous manipulation policy on a generic object reposing task, then post-trains downstream policies with this pretrained behavior as a prior on contact-rich downstream tasks. This enables learning new behaviors that are otherwise difficult to discover from scratch on multi-fingered robots. We find that the pretrained policy generalizes and can solve the reposing phase of downstream tasks zero-shot. However, naive RL fine-tuning rapidly degrades this capability during task transfer. To address this, we propose a post-training framework that combines behavior-cloning distillation to adapt the actor to new observations, frozen-actor critic warm-up to calibrate it on the downstream reward, and conservative on-policy updates to prevent large policy drift. To safely exploit the full kinematic dexterity of an arm-hand robot, we introduce a joint configuration-space Geometric Fabric controller that mediates between the RL policy and the robot. Finally, we distill the post-trained teacher into a stereo-RGB student policy that zero-shot sim-to-real transfers on a 23 DoF Kuka-Allegro robot. The resulting system solves contact-rich, long-horizon manipulation tasks requiring grasping, reorienting, and insertion across a wide range of initial states.
